headline: Your 4-week routine with 2% Salicylic Acid
subhead: Apply 2-3 drops after cleansing & toning, in the PM.
footnote: Brand consumer studies: 97% subjects felt less oily after 2 weeks; 90% subjects noticed visible skin clarity in 4 weeks. Frames are AI illustrations, not real results.
layout_description: Transformation journey (template #14 Progress / timeline): headline top, three progress frames of the same AI-illustrated skin area left to right (Day 1, Week 2, Week 4), each label tied to a cited study line; small real pack shot bottom-right; AI-GENERATED — ILLUSTRATIVE badge; study footnote.
image_prompt: Background only: off-white tabletop and matte wall, soft light from the upper left. Keep the top 30% calm and empty for the headline copy and an empty clear space at the lower right for a product photo placed later. No product, no bottle, no packaging, no text, no letters, no logos, no people, no faces, no skin, no hands.
photography_needed: Real, consented progress photos from the brand's own 4-week consumer study (same person, same light, Day 1 / Week 2 / Week 4) to replace the AI frames before any use.
adaptation_notes: User request 2026-10-03: transformation-journey format (progress frames rather than before/after wording), flagged Severe. Frame labels use only the page's study wording and timeframes (F17: less oily at 2 weeks; F15: visible clarity at 4 weeks); no 'acne gone' or cure wording. Frames are AI illustrations and carry the visible AI mark; not exportable until real study photos replace them.
warnings: Model (AI person, hands or skin frames) used: Severe by default (user rule 2026-10-04). Kept for review; not exportable until real, consented photos replace the AI images.

verdict.label: Fix before review
verdict.detail: Change the flagged lines, or attach the substantiation a reviewer would need to accept them.

findings.message: Statistics need their study qualifier on the creative and must not be worded more strongly than the study.
findings.fix: Quote the stat exactly as the study states it ('90% subjects said…') and add a footnote: study type (consumer perception / in-vivo / in-vitro), duration, and n if known.

findings.message: A time-bound result needs a study of that duration, with the qualifier shown on the creative.
findings.fix: Keep the timeframe only if it comes from a study you can cite, and put the qualifier in the footnote (e.g. '*Consumer perception study, 4 weeks'). Otherwise remove the timeframe.
